questions.question: The sun comes up every morning. Is this always, sometimes, or never?
questions.explain: The sun comes up every single morning, so it is always. We do not need to wish for it to happen.

questions.question: Can a fish fly like a bird? Always, sometimes, or never?
questions.explain: A fish cannot fly, so it is never. Wishing it could does not change what a fish can do.

questions.question: It can rain in summer in BC. Is this always, sometimes, or never?
questions.explain: Summer rain happens in BC, but not every day. That makes it sometimes, not always or never.

questions.question: You close your eyes. Do you always stop seeing?
questions.explain: Every time you close your eyes, you stop seeing, so it is always. It does not depend on the time of day.

questions.question: Max pulls a ball from a box full of red balls. Is it always, sometimes, or never red?
questions.explain: Every ball in the box is red, so he always gets a red one. There is no other colour to find.

questions.question: A bag has 8 red balls and 2 blue balls. You pick one blind. Is it always, sometimes, or never red?
questions.explain: Most balls are red, but there are blue ones too, so it is sometimes. A likely thing is not the same as a sure thing.

questions.question: Layla says: I will wish hard tonight, so tomorrow it will always be sunny. What went wrong?
questions.explain: A sunny day is a sometimes thing. Wishing does not turn a sometimes into an always.

questions.question: A box has 9 red balls and 1 blue ball. You pick one blind. Is it always, sometimes, or never blue?
options: Never, red is all there is
questions.explain: There is one blue ball in the box, so it is sometimes, not never. Having 9 red does not make blue impossible.

questions.question: A jar has 10 blue marbles. Mia picks one and says it is sometimes red. Is she right?
options: Yes, red might be in there
questions.explain: There are only blue marbles in the jar, so it is always blue. Mia is calling a sure thing a maybe thing.

questions.question: Ben rides the school bus. He wants the seat by the window. Getting the window seat is never, sometimes, or always?
options: Never, the bus is too full
questions.explain: Some days the window seat is free and some days another kid takes it, so it is sometimes. Liking that seat a lot does not make it always.

questions.question: Mia's dad packs one fruit in her lunch each day. Today Mia hopes it is a peach. Finding a peach in her lunch is never, sometimes, or always?
questions.explain: Dad picks the fruit, so a peach can come on some days and not on others. That is sometimes, even when Mia hopes hard for it.

questions.question: Ella's dog Rex barks a lot. Ella wants Rex to talk to her in words. Rex saying words is never, sometimes, or always?
questions.explain: Dogs can bark, but they cannot say words, so this never happens. Wishing for something does not make it possible.
